newsitem.title: USA: U.S. looks to APEC for market opening opportunities.
newsitem.headline: U.S. looks to APEC for market opening opportunities.

text.p: U.S. trade officials hope their counterparts from Asia-Pacific nations will take steps toward new trade agreements this week similar to a successful pact to end tariffs on computers and other high-technology gear.
Trade ministers from the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum will gather in Montreal, Quebec, on Thursday and Friday to discuss a number of trade issues.
The meeting will provide an opportunity to test the waters for a new round of tariff cuts on wood, paper and other products and also for negotiation on financial services, U.S. officials said.

"This is something we have a considerable interest in," one U.S. trade official said. "We have heard that some of the other parties would also be interested in seeing if we could identify some areas or get some work going which would lead to greater liberalisation in a fairly timely manner."

The official said the success of an agreement to eliminate tariffs on computers, software and other high-tech gear by 2000 inspired ministers to look for other areas of trade liberalisation that could be supported by the diverse membership of APEC.

It was APEC that gave the information technology agreement a much needed shot in the arm last year and cleared the way for a final deal at a meeting of World Trade Organisation trade ministers in December.
"We'll be interested in other ideas countries might have," one U.S. official said.

Canada has been pushing for a round of trade liberalisation on environmental products and services and an official said last week that Canada found support for the idea among its major trading partners. Canadian Trade Minister Art Eggleton met last week in Toronto with his counterparts from the United States, Japan and European Union during a meeting of the so-called "Quad" trading partners.
The U.S. official said the APEC trade ministers will be examining the possibilities at this week's meeting.
"At this point, things are at the exploratory stage. We would like to give that a nudge if the other parties are interested," the U.S. official said.
"As to what the chances are (of identifying an area), it is unclear at this point. But we think there are some areas where there might be a broad consensus."

The official said the APEC ministers also would probably discuss global negotiations to open financial services markets. The finance ministers at a meeting earlier this year backed a plan to complete negotiations by the end of the year.
The ministers also are likely to discuss individual efforts to speed up trade liberalisation within APEC.

The trade ministers meeting will lay the groundwork for a meeting of leaders in November in Vancouver, British Columbia. APEC includes Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
